What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing. Needs: network: working loopback.
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at Zend/zend_execute_API.c:389 in _zval_ptr_dtor when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 09881626498d, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/http_fopen_wrapper.c:197-201 (free at :201). Claimed ":263" is the line number in the 2005 fix commit's tree, NOT in php-5.0.0.
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as history-5x-stdext (historical-known, confidence high).

platform_precondition.needs: select() rejects a timeval whose tv_usec is out of range (EINVAL) rather than sleeping on it

platform_precondition_why: PHP 5.0.0's liveness check (main/streams/xp_socket.c, PHP_STREAM_OPTION_CHECK_LIVENESS) sets only tv.tv_sec of the timeval it hands to select(); tv_usec is whatever the stack held. Linux rejects such a timeval: glibc passes it to the kernel, which answers EINVAL, PHP reads the socket as alive and the script runs to its end, where the use-after-free this case records is reached (the corpus's native oracle). musl 1.2.5's select (src/select/select.c) folds an out-of-range tv_usec into the seconds instead -- `s += us/1000000` -- so a positive garbage tv_usec becomes a timeout of hours or days and the script hangs before its defect, on whichever arms and images leave such a value on the stack (measured 2026-10-28: the un-instrumented image hangs on the nested arms, a diagnostic image with extra stack use completes and the nested arms catch the defect at ASan's own site, _zval_ptr_dtor). Checked, not asserted: ports/php/app/probe-timeval.c runs on every arm.
